question.:question/problem:
What is the sum of the leading entries of the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & -3 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd rows of $A$ are $-3$, $5$, and $2$, respectively.

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & -3 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$

So, the answer is $-3+5+2=4.$

What is the sum of the leading entries of the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}8 & -6 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & -5 & -1 \\ -1 & 4 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd rows of $A$ are $8$, $3$, and $-5$, respectively.

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}8 & -6 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & -5 & -1 \\ -1 & 4 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}
$$

So, the answer is $8+3+(-5)=6.$

What is the sum of the leading entries of the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 & -6 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -5 \\ -7 & -9 & 3 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & -8 & -2\end{bmatrix}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd rows of $A$ are $1$, $-5$, and $-7$, respectively.

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 & -6 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -5 \\ -7 & -9 & 3 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & -8 & -2\end{bmatrix}
$$

So, the answer is $1+(-5)+(-7)=-11.$

What is the sum of the leading entries of the $1$st, $3$rd, and $4$th rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 3 & 3 & -5 \\ 0 & -8 & -7 & -5 \\ 0 & 8 & -3 & 3 \\ 6 & 6 & 5 & 3\end{bmatrix}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $1$st, $3$rd, and $4$th rows of $A$ are $3$, $8$, and $6$, respectively.

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 3 & 3 & -5 \\ 0 & -8 & -7 & -5 \\ 0 & 8 & -3 & 3 \\ 6 & 6 & 5 & 3\end{bmatrix}
$$

So, the answer is $3+8+6=17.$

What is the sum of the leading entries of the $2$nd, $3$rd, and $4$th rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 5 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & -6 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -3\end{bmatrix}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $2$nd, $3$rd, and $4$th rows of $A$ are $4$, $-6$, and $2$, respectively.

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 5 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & -6 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -3\end{bmatrix}
$$

So, the answer is $4+(-6)+2=0.$
